<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowExpressions))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowExpressions))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowExpressions))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowExpressions))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df4c06e6b165bb0a30eb86e4ace6258932f69d8a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1769ef19ed0cecfd179beb01bab0cb6f742be532` — the merge of head `9fe18676371e491a5b842d595750eee0a645cf53` into base `df4c06e6b165bb0a30eb86e4ace6258932f69d8a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1769ef19ed0cecfd179beb01bab0cb6f742be532 && git checkout 1769ef19ed0cecfd179beb01bab0cb6f742be532
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin df4c06e6b165bb0a30eb86e4ace6258932f69d8a 9fe18676371e491a5b842d595750eee0a645cf53 && git checkout -B drift-repro df4c06e6b165bb0a30eb86e4ace6258932f69d8a && git merge --no-ff 9fe18676371e491a5b842d595750eee0a645cf53

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df4c06e6b165bb0a30eb86e4ace6258932f69d8a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs df4c06e6b165bb0a30eb86e4ace6258932f69d8a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 按时间触发的流程（time-relative），注册时的字段检查改为对照它实际扫描的对象（`timeRelative.object`），不再对照开始节点上的 `objectName`；MCP `validate_expression` 的说明和 SKILL.md 同步改为"把被扫描的对象作为 objectName 传入"。
- **为什么改：** 原来两对象的旧流程会对正确字段报 `unknown field`、对运行时必失败的字段反而不报，只写了 `timeRelative.object` 的流程完全不检查（#30396，PR #30393 复审的跟进项）。
- **风险与回滚：** 只影响注册时记在日志里的提示（从不抛错），以及 MCP 工具的说明文字；工具的输入和判定不变。回滚即撤本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts` `validateFlowExpressions` 里取对象的那几行。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/flow-registration-checks.test.ts`。
- **需要您做的：** 无，席位经合并队列落地（非受管面，147 行，非 BREAKING）。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT。席位按 TIER_DEFAULT 读完 diff，取对象改走引擎自己的 `deriveTriggerBinding`，只影响注册日志提示和 MCP 说明文字；engine.ts 的 4 行偏差接受，与席位 3 的 #30055 已对好先后。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#2 · head `9fe18676371e491a5b842d595750eee0a645cf53`

- **形态:** draft, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`), no assignee, no review request; 6 files, +131 −16 against merge base `fdd06415`; `check-governed-merges --pr 30453`: NOT governed (0 of 6 paths), 147 lines ≤ 3000. Title has no `!`.
- **Review face:** `TIER_DEFAULT` (declaration face: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; no schema, no governed path, no narrowing), written here by the seat.
- **Seat read (diff against `fdd06415`):** `validateFlowExpressions` now reads the bound object off `deriveTriggerBinding` — `binding.object` when `triggerType === 'time_relative'`, the start node's `config.objectName` otherwise — the same answer the run and `activateFlowTrigger` use, not a second reading of the start node. Derived only when `advisory && objectSchemaResolver`; the stored pass (`advisory: false`) never reads the hint, so it is untouched. `deriveTriggerBinding` already runs on the same registration path (`validateApiTriggerSecret`), so no new throw path enters registration; the warnings stay logged, never thrown, and the fatal set is unchanged. Every non-time-relative flow is typed exactly as before.
- **Deviation accepted:** `engine.ts` +4 (one host wiring line `deriveTriggerBinding` in the `validateFlowExpressions` host, three docblock lines). Needed because that host is built in `engine.ts`; outside the ordered file list and outside the forbidden set. Ordering with seat 3's `engine.ts` move (#30055) agreed: this PR lands first; #30055 moves six other methods and does not touch `validateFlowExpressions`.
- **MCP text:** `validate_expression` description, the `sweepObject` input text and `skill-md.ts` no longer present "sweepObject other than objectName" as a supported shape; they name the publish refusal `flow-time-relative-object-mismatch` (PR #30393). Inputs and verdicts unchanged (schema text only). True against the head.
- **Pins:** four cases on the real `AutomationEngine.registerFlow` — two-object stored flow (swept-object field passes; start-object-only field warns), one-object flow unchanged (typo still warns), sweep-only flow now typed. Dev ablation: 3 red, restored.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in PR body and changeset; `patch` ×2 (`@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/mcp`).
- **Dev readings (`9fe18676`):** service-automation 3418/3418, mcp 678/678, typecheck and `pnpm lint` green, derived gates 62/62, full dogfood 419 files / 3492 passed. os-dev-report 6657502054.
- **门禁 check-runs:** in progress at ACCEPT; auto-merge waits on the required contexts. `main` moved 19 commits past the merge base, none under `packages/services/service-automation` or `packages/mcp`; the merge queue tests the merged result.
- **落地条款:** Fixes #30396. Ordinary queue landing by this seat: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` on this head.
